Al Sadu (UAE): Urgent Safeguarding List 2011 (6.COM 8.21); Representative List 2025 (20.COM 7.c.1, transfer).
The "Safeguarding programme for Al Sadu" (2011–2023) entered the Register of Good Safeguarding Practices in 2025; photos "© Intangible Heritage Department (ADACH)".
UNESCO's file says "a dwindling number of older women" keep the practice; girls "learn by watching".

"Traditional weaving of Al Sadu" (Saudi Arabia, Kuwait) was inscribed in 2020 (15.COM 8.b.4). In 2025 the Committee inscribed it on an extended basis to include Qatar (20.COM 7.b.54); the new file, No. 02158, "incorporates and replaces" the 2020 entry.
Kuwait's Al Sadu Project began in 1978 as a private initiative and became the Al Sadu Weaving Cooperative Society in 1991.
Lorimer's *Gazetteer* (1908, 1915) followed Curzon's 1903 tour; its map was drawn to be "fitted alongside the map of India"; its genealogies omitted women.
Creative Australia's First Nations protocols (third edition, 2020, Terri Janke) set ten principles, including self-determination and interpretation.

From 2006, ten Zuni artists made about two dozen map paintings for the A:shiwi A:wan Museum and Heritage Center, shown at the Fowler Museum in 2015–16. The museum's own page gives "sixteen Zuni artists" and "thirty-one map art paintings" in the exhibition; counts differ by date.

EMKP's Great Zimbabwe project (2020SG08), led by Munyaradzi Elton Sagiya and hosted by National Museums and Monuments of Zimbabwe, recorded dry-stone masons' knowledge (fieldwork March–April 2021; published 12 July 2024).
